caption:
There haven’t been many better PG’s in college basketball this season than 6’6 NC State Guard Quadir Copeland 

Copeland has had a strong season where he’s averaging 14/4/6 on 59/54/76 splits. 

Copeland has a strong mix of athleticism, finishing, passing, and craft that not many 6’6 players possess which helps him impact the game at a strong level. Copeland has been one of the best guard finishers in college basketball shooting 68% at the rim and has excelled in the PNR and as a driver. Copeland uses his ability to create at the rim to create plays for his teammates at a high level and he also has strong passing vision. 

Copeland and LaBaron Philon are the only players in college basketball this season who have an AST% of 35, and is shooting 60% at the rim on 40 makes as well.

caption: After two years at Nc State, I can confidently say I’m a changed man. Not in ways I would’ve expected though.  Before the last two years of my life, the root of my happiness was my performance on the field and what others thought about me, always trying to prove people wrong and trying to be the best at the sport I could be. However, as I came to know Christ more clear I realized how wrong I had been this whole time. I wasn’t meant to play this game with the sole purpose of being the best at it. I was meant to show others just how awesome a relationship with Jesus Christ can be through my actions, words, and how I play.  There is always someone watching what you do and how you interact with others even in your worst and best moments. So, as I plan to leave Nc State for my future years of football, I am forever grateful for those who helped me grow in my faith and for everyone I came in contact with.  Romans 1:16

caption:
if you know me at all you know how much i love this sport and i have always dreaded this part. volleyball has brought me so many amazing memories and to places all over, but most importantly this sport has truly given me my best friends. i do not know where i would be as a person without every teammate, coach, support staff, etc that has come into my life. and a special thank you to NC State Volleyball for the past 3 years as i was able to develop so much on and off the court. i’m thankful for it all. whether that be the loud cheers in a packed Reynolds gym or dance parties in the locker room or even the hard conditioning mornings… i would not change a thing about my experience. 

God has blessed me with not only the ability but especially the passion to play this sport and i am forever grateful i could glorify Him through it all. no matter what my next step is, He will guide me with the same love, dedication, and strength. Thank you volleyball.

“Then I heard a voice of the Lord asking: Who will I send? Who will go for us? I said: Here I am Lord. Send me.” - Isaiah 6:8

Thank you Jesus for letting us see a glimpse of your glory in Uganda this past week.  What an honor it is to serve you, Jesus. It was a joy to be surrounded with people full of the love of God, and laughter. From the joy, tears, and countless prayers shared, I will be forever thankful.

The Lord was so kind to let us experience His love through His people in Kampala. The countless testimonies we heard revealed His faithfulness and compassion. Through street evangelism, discipleship, and Bible studies, we got to witness the power of His Holy Spirit as well as His kindness. Thank you Shannon for showing us what it means to be fully obedient and dependent on the Lord; surrendering to what the Lord is calling you to do. 

What a beautiful experience to witness people surrendering to Jesus, and entering into new life with Him! The Lord is good and His grace is sufficient 🤍

caption:
Our Heavenly Father is kind, loving, caring, accepting, and forgiving. This past week at UTC is one that I will never forget. I learned so much; He gives me the strength to do everything. Know that you are never alone and that God is always with you, even when you don’t think He is. He protects and satisfies me. I am enough, and He is my Why (I belong to Him). I proclaim that I Am a Child of God, and there is nothing I desire more than Christ. I can now be free, knowing that He is WITH me.

As an athlete, I often look to my sport to validate my existence and my worthiness; however, this week I learned that that isn’t true. Our Father just wants ME/US (He loves us all). Our worth isn’t found in our performance and what others think about us, but rather in what God says about us... we are significant.

“For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them.”
‭‭Ephesians‬ ‭2‬:‭10‬ ‭ESV‬‬
